NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 6 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 18 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 18, 12:11 AM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 6 DraftKings main slate at 22.7 DraftKings points for $7,500, at Las Vegas. Matthew Stafford (21.2, $6,400) and Drake Maye (20.4, $6,600) are next.

Tyler Huntley returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.60 projected points per $1,000 at $4,700.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 18, 12:11 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 6

Josh Allen, BUF at LV ($7,500)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.7 DraftKings points at $7,500, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.5 points clear of Matthew Stafford. The model includes 6.8 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.03 projected points per $1,000, 14th of 17 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.7 points with a simulated floor of 8.7 and a ceiling of 41.7, and he holds 10% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 5.5-point favorite on the road against Las Vegas, with an implied team total of 29.5 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Matthew Stafford, LAR vs ARI ($6,400)

Matthew Stafford projects 2nd at the position with 21.2 DraftKings points at $6,400. The salary works out to 3.32 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 17 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Stafford averaged 21.2 points with a simulated floor of 8.3 and a ceiling of 38.7, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Rams are a 12.5-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 32 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Tyler Huntley, BAL at CLE ($4,700)

Tyler Huntley projects for 16.9 DraftKings points at $4,700, which works out to 3.60 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 17 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.6 rushing attempts. Across 50,000 simulations Huntley averaged 16.9 points with a simulated floor of 6.5 and a ceiling of 31.1, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Baltimore is a 3-point favorite on the road against Cleveland, with an implied team total of 21.25 in a game totaled at 39.5.
